title: Evidence Promotion Became a Mechanical Governance Boundary
summary: The existing Claim → Evidence → Verification → Oscar chain now has a deterministic promotion ladder that distinguishes eligibility from canonical promotion and blocks stale, superseded, conflicting, wrong-commit, missing-provenance, forbidden-source, and production-unsupported promotion.
what_happened: A small promotion runtime was added on top of the existing evidence authority chain. Fresh CI on PR #37 ran ten Claim/Evidence tests, thirteen Oscar tests, thirteen promotion tests, exact-head verification, Oscar challenge, and current evidence evaluation; the machine-readable artifact bound the result to commit d5109097d3fec5ddebf75c3a6dd5ee43eab12448.
what_we_learned: Eligibility must not silently become canonical truth.
Current evidence must match the exact commit and remain non-superseded.
Conflicting current evidence must block promotion rather than allow a convenient PASS to win.
Production-safe requires production evidence; test or documentation evidence cannot establish production safety.
Oscar acceptance is a gate in the existing authority chain, not a replacement for explicit governance promotion.
why_it_matters: This closes the remaining gap between something being independently accepted and something being allowed to become canonical state, while preserving one authority chain.
what_changed: Extended Claim Evidence CI to run Oscar and promotion tests and evaluate current evidence through the promotion boundary.
Defined UNVERIFIED → BUILDER_VERIFIED → OSCAR_ACCEPTED → CANONICAL_VERIFIED → PRODUCTION_SAFE.
Required explicit promotion decisions for canonical and production promotion.
next_best_action: Maintain the promotion boundary as the gate for every future claim and add production evidence only when a real production claim is being evaluated.
